§9.1.4 Header-Only Tables

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-header-only-tables · tables degenerate failure-mode

✅ Normative

The output MUST NOT contain a table that is a header with no body. A header row MUST either be rendered together with its body or, where no body can be joined to it, rendered as ordinary text — never as an orphan header row standing as a table.

The failure: a header row becomes a table of its own while the rows it describes end up in a neighbouring region as plain text. The result claims there is a table with no data in it, and separately claims there is a run of loose numbers with no meaning.

Emitted:   | Duration | Factor |     ← header-only table…

           1   0.94                  ← …its body rendered as plain text
           2   0.91                    from the neighbouring region

Joining a header to its body

A header row with no rows under it belongs to the body immediately below or beside it. The header and body MUST be rendered as one table only when all three hold:

  • the body is immediately adjacent — the next thing on the page, not across a gap of other content;
  • the column bounds match — the body's columns line up under the header's;
  • nothing sits in between — no paragraph, no other table, no unrelated band.

If any condition fails, the merge MUST NOT be made (never invent): the stray header line MUST be rendered as text rather than as a one-row table.

How large a gap is too large is not fixed. A gap large enough to put the adjacency in doubt counts as a failed condition, and the header is not merged.

The related shape

A single row of labels on its own is not a table. Neither is a small table folded into the middle of another table's body — see Side-by-Side Mini Tables§9.2.8 for that one.

The one exception

A blank pre-printed form is headers plus empty rows, and there the structure genuinely is the content: it MUST be rendered, rows included — see Empty Pre-Printed Grids§9.1.3. That case has a body of printed empty rows. It is not a header standing alone.

Related

  • Split Tables Sharing a Header§9.2.9 — when a header legitimately covers fragments with a gap
  • Empty Pre-Printed Grids§9.1.3 — the one case where headers plus empty rows are the whole content
  • Side-by-Side Mini Tables§9.2.8 — a small table inside another's body
  • Is This Even a Table§9.1.5 — a lone label row fails the relation test
